title: Webb finds the dwarf galaxy behind the farthest fast radio burst
description:
A fast radio burst detected in 2024 left its galaxy just 3 billion years after the big bang, the most distant one seen to date. In a peer-reviewed paper published Oct. 8, 2026, astronomers report that the James Webb Space Telescope found its host where ground telescopes saw nothing: a dwarf galaxy 1,000 times less massive than they expected. The team says that makes a neutron star merger a very unlikely source, but what makes these bursts is still unknown.
